meta.description: Audit, revise, or draft manuscript statistical reporting for Nature/high-impact journals. Nine-step workflow (classify task → extract design → define n/replication → map claims to analyses → check failure modes → check reporting completeness → align figure statistics → draft/revise → QA). Enforces design transparency, independent experimental unit as default n, effect sizes + uncertainty over significance-only, AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED for missing info. Covers nested data, multiple comparisons, biological vs technical replicates, randomization, blinding, figure-legend statistics.

scientific_integrity.detail: Does not invent p values, sample sizes, tests, corrections, exclusion rules. Marks AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED. Separates what was measured, what unit analyzed, what inference claimed. Does not upgrade association to mechanism/causality. Does not hide non-significant results.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for statistical reporting review. Not substitute for statistician reanalysis unless user supplies data. Does not give medical/regulatory advice beyond reporting. Bounded audit when input partial. Independent experimental unit as default n (not cells/fields).

methodological_ground.detail: Design transparency principle sound. Effect sizes + uncertainty preferred over significance-only. Claims-to-analyses mapping rigorous. Common failure modes taxonomy (nested data, many comparisons, interaction claims, correlations) evidence-based. Figure-statistics alignment comprehensive.

code_usability.detail: Nine-step workflow clear. Output format structured (scope, major issues with P0/P1/P2, ready-to-paste revision, AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED, reviewer-risk). On-demand references for failure modes, reporting completeness, figure stats, reviewer checklist, Nature requirements, NMI format.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive: audit, rewrite, draft, reviewer-response, figure-statistics alignment, data-backed reanalysis. Design extraction (groups, treatments, endpoints, blocking, randomization, blinding, exclusions). n/replication definition (independent units vs tech replicates). Claims-to-analyses mapping. Journal-specific (Nature flagship, NMI). Minor: no explicit power analysis guidance.

reliability.note: Excellent red lines: does not invent p values/sample sizes/tests/corrections. Independent unit principle enforced (not cells/images as independent). Does not upgrade association to causality. Does not hide non-significant results. AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED for missing info. Bounded audit when partial input. Final QA with reviewer-checklist.

performance_context.note: Efficient on-demand loading: common-failure-modes, statistical-reporting, figure-statistics, reviewer-checklist, nature-article-requirements, NMI format loaded only when needed. Bounded audit for partial input (clear scope statement).

agent_usability.note: Clear nine-step workflow. Default stance principles explicit. Output format structured with severity labels (P0/P1/P2). Red lines comprehensive (6 prohibitions). Source hierarchy defined. Minor: lacks decision tree for classifying task mode (audit vs rewrite vs draft vs reviewer-response).

human_usability.note: Strong bilingual support (Chinese academic drafts, 统计审查 trigger). Ready-to-paste revision output. AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED section clear. Reviewer-risk note valuable. Reporting notes for clean drafts. Severity labels (P0/P1/P2) prioritize fixes.

security.note: Excellent boundaries: does not invent statistical details. Does not give medical/regulatory advice beyond reporting. Does not recommend tests when design unclear. Separates significance from importance/causality. AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED explicit marking.

maintainability.note: Good modular design: nine-step workflow, on-demand references (6 files), source hierarchy. Shared consistency-sweep from nature-shared. Journal-specific requirements cleanly isolated. Minor: lacks version tracking for statistical guidelines (ICMJE, CONSORT, ARRIVE versions evolve).

agent_specific.note: Strong principles: independent experimental unit, effect sizes + uncertainty. Claims-to-analyses mapping sophisticated. Common failure modes taxonomy. Minor: no explicit token budget for very long Methods (50+ statistical tests). Data-backed reanalysis mentioned but workflow not detailed. Figure-statistics alignment documented but automation unclear (manual check vs script validation).

key_strengths: Exceptional independent experimental unit principle: default n is independent unit (not cells/images/fields), prevents pseudoreplication, enforced via design extraction
Strong non-invention discipline: marks AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED for missing randomization/blinding/sample sizes/tests/corrections instead of fabricating
Comprehensive failure-mode taxonomy: nested data, multiple comparisons, interaction claims, correlation/regression, outliers, tiny samples with evidence-based detection
Robust claims-to-analyses mapping: for each result claim, records comparison/model, test family, assumptions, correction, effect estimate, uncertainty, exact p-value policy
Sophisticated figure-statistics alignment: checks legend text, error bars, stars, box/violin plots, source data n, panel labels for consistency

recommendations.title: Add task-mode classification decision tree
recommendations.problem: Workflow step 1 says 'classify task' (audit vs rewrite vs draft vs reviewer-response vs figure-alignment vs data-reanalysis) but no decision tree. Agent must infer mode from user request without structured guidance.
recommendations.root_cause: Task classification documented as step but classification logic not explicit.
recommendations.fix: Add references/task-mode-decision-tree.md: (1) flowchart: if user provides existing text → audit, if reviewer comment → reviewer-response, if figure only → figure-alignment, if data + request → data-reanalysis, if nothing → draft; (2) mode-specific workflow variations (audit: extract → check → revise, draft: define → map → write); (3) mode transition rules (audit discovering missing design → switch to AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED mode). Include in workflow step 1.

recommendations.title: Add concrete re-statement examples for correction method fixes
recommendations.problem: Multiple comparison correction mismatch flagged (stated Bonferroni, applied Holm-Bonferroni) with recommendation 'clarify method or re-state results' but no concrete example of re-stated results. User must figure out how to present corrected P values.
recommendations.root_cause: Fix recommendations abstract (what to do) not concrete (example text).
recommendations.fix: Enhance common-failure-modes.md multiple-comparison section: (1) add before/after examples for correction method fixes (stated Bonferroni, critical P=0.05/15=0.0033 → Holm-Bonferroni, adjusted P values: 0.002, 0.015, 0.031), (2) include table format for presenting adjusted P values, (3) legend wording templates ('P values adjusted for multiple comparisons using Holm-Bonferroni method'). Provide concrete example in ready-to-paste revision.

recommendations.title: Add reviewer-risk pre-emptive response suggestions
recommendations.problem: Reviewer-risk note identifies potential challenges (sample size justification missing, outlier exclusion criteria not pre-specified) but no pre-emptive response suggestions. User must draft responses from scratch when reviewer raises issue.
recommendations.root_cause: Reviewer-checklist focuses on risk identification, not response preparation.
recommendations.fix: Enhance reviewer-checklist.md with response templates: (1) for each common risk (sample size, outlier exclusion, correction method), provide response template acknowledging limitation and mitigation ('Sample size was based on preliminary experiments showing effect size d=1.2; post-hoc power analysis confirms >80% power; we acknowledge lack of formal a priori calculation'), (2) include references to add (cite power analysis paper, pre-registration standard). Generate 'Pre-emptive reviewer responses' section in output after reviewer-risk note.
